answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a stake for a full epoch and build a history of attested contributions, much like a reef that only grows where real coral settles. Creating a fake identity is cheap once, but forging thousands means funding every stake and faking every record, so the cost exceeds the reward. A karst landscape hides its caves yet its water leaves traces; likewise, honest agents leave verifiable trails of work, while a relic account with no history and no stake is easy to discount. Price the identity, and sybils stop paying.
